aggregation: MicroSeries.sum and MicroSeries.groupby(source household).sum on analysis flags in each part's frozen simulation, with map_to='person' for residents; stored weight columns are not read.

conventions.candidate_rank: Candidates are ranked within their household by person ID (expanded_job_rank); the raise test instead takes the household's two highest earners by market income.
conventions.fall: Households (and their residents) in the full group but not the narrower one; adults flagged in the full group but not the narrower one. Narrowing the job test can move a household from strict to additional, so the additional group is not bounded by its full count.
conventions.groups: strict: households below 0% retention on any test in the set; additional: below 50% and not below 0% on any test; below_half: below 50%. Residents counted once.
conventions.health: with_health: government-valued health coverage, ACA premium tax credit counted once (d_net_single_ptc); without_health: every part of net income except health benefits and costs (d_net_without_health).
conventions.job_test: A candidate (aged 18-64; no wages or self-employment income; not a full-time student; not reporting disability) takes a full-time job (40 hours x 52 weeks) at the state's 2017 minimum wage, one candidate at a time.
conventions.largest_loss: The part of net income whose change lowers household resources most for the flagged adult's own test (cliffs2017.decompose.primary_driver), with the premium tax credit counted once (the marketplace premium left out, as driver_intervals.largest_loss does). A raise worker flagged by several raises takes the smallest such raise. EITC is not separable: it is inside household_refundable_tax_credits.
conventions.units: adults: flagged adults (or candidates); households; household_members: residents of those households.

definitional_gaps: Census counts people who did not work at all in the year by their own main reason; the job test's candidates have no wages or self-employment income in the model's 2017 data and are not flagged as full-time students or as having a disability (is_full_time_student, is_disabled). A person with a disability who names another main reason stays in the Census rows after removing 'ill or disabled', and a person who names illness without a disability flag is a candidate.

Census combines going to school with other reasons, so only bounds match the candidate pool: removing 'ill or disabled' alone keeps every student (upper comparator); removing 'school or other' too also drops non-students who gave other reasons (lower comparator).

Both keep retirees aged 18-64 who report no disability: the 2017 table counts 7.5 million adults aged 18-64 who did not work and named retirement, 5.7 million of them aged 55-64. The table has no 62-64 row.
Census weights CPS ASEC respondents; the model counts the calibrated Microcosm households of the 2017 run, whose own calibration need not match these tables.
external_benchmark.not_used: Brookings' 'Meet the out-of-work' (2017) covers 130 cities and counties, not the nation.

medicaid_expansion.how_read: The 2017 run's own tax-benefit system, at 1 January 2017, the instant the Medicaid adult formula (is_adult_for_medicaid_fc) reads for a 2017 period. The parameter's earliest dated values are 1 January 2018; policyengine-us backdates each parameter's earliest value to 2015, so the 2017 run applies the January 2018 limits. A state covers the ACA adult group when its limit is at least 1.38 (138% of poverty); a positive limit below 1.38 (Wisconsin's 1.00) covers adults below it under a waiver without expanding; a null limit stands for the model's -inf, no adult group.
